Current international law can regulate AWS responsibly while allowing strategic use.</jats:p>\", \"URL\": \"https://doi.org/10.69790/epis-rep-aic-1/39949\", \"published\": {\"date-parts\": [[2025, 10, 15]]}}, {\"DOI\": \"10.2139/ssrn.6238401\", \"title\": [\"Registering the Machine: A Framework for Autonomous Agent Accountability\"], \"abstract\": \"<jats:p><p>Autonomous AI agents represent a regulatory inflection point comparable to the introduction of motor vehicles, aircraft, or securities markets—each of which eventually required a registration system.&nbsp;&nbsp;<span>They exhibit characteristics that distinguish them from traditional software: persistence, autonomy, and goal-directedness. They operate continuously, make decisions without human approval at each step, and adapt their behavior based on environmental feedback.
